entries.meaning: Garuda asks Bhushundi seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest pain and joy, the innate natures of saint and non-saint, the highest scriptural merit, the most terrible sin and the diseases of mind. Bhushundi answers that no body equals the human, desired by all moving and unmoving beings: it is a stairway to hell, heaven or liberation and gives knowledge, detachment and devotion. One who gains it yet does not worship Hari trades the philosopher's stone in hand for glass. No misery equals poverty and no worldly happiness equals meeting saints. Saints naturally benefit others through thought, word and body, enduring hardship for others like the generous birch tree that yields its bark. The wicked cause others' pain, binding them like flax even as its own skin is stripped; without gain they harm like a snake and mouse whose attack destroys both; they ruin another's prosperity and perish like hail that destroys crops and melts. Their rise torments the world like an ill-omened comet, while a saint's rise continually brings joy like the world-blessing moon. The Vedas declare nonviolence the highest dharma and no sin as heavy as slander. Reviling Hari and guru leads repeatedly to frog-birth, reviling Brahmins through hells to crow-birth, reviling gods and scripture to Raurava, delighting in slander of saints to owl-birth and slandering everyone to bat-birth. Delusion is the root of all mental illness: desire is wind-disorder, limitless greed phlegm and anger burning bile; together they form a painful systemic fever. Sense ambitions are countless thorns; possessiveness is ringworm, envy itching, joy and grief throat diseases, burning at another's happiness consumption, and wicked crookedness leprosy. Ego is a painful tumour; hypocrisy, deceit, pride and conceit disorders of the nerves; craving severe abdominal swelling; the three cravings a recurrent fever; jealousy and lack of discernment are double fevers. The catalogue of maladies is endless.

All beings are sick in this way, afflicted by grief, joy, fear, attachment and separation. Bhushundi has named only some mental diseases; everyone has them, though few recognize them. Recognition weakens these enemies but does not wholly destroy them, and the wrong diet of sense objects makes them sprout again—even in a sage's heart. Rama's grace destroys every disease when the right conjunction arises: trust in the true guru-physician's words, restraint and absence of craving for sense objects; devotion to Raghupati as the life-restoring herb, taken with a mind filled by faith. The mind is known to be healthy when detachment grows strong, the fresh hunger of good understanding increases and weakness for sense objects is gone; bathed in the clear water of knowledge, it becomes pervaded by Rama-devotion. Shiva, Brahma, Shuka, Sanaka, Narada and other contemplative sages agree: love Rama's lotus feet. Veda, Purana and all texts say there is no happiness without Raghupati-devotion. A tortoise may grow hair, a barren woman's child may kill someone, flowers may bloom in the sky, thirst may be quenched by mirage-water, a hare may grow horns, darkness may destroy the sun and fire may arise from snow—but a being opposed to Rama cannot find happiness. Butter might come from churning water and oil from sand, yet without worshipping Hari no one crosses becoming: this principle cannot be overturned. The Lord can make a gnat Brahma and reduce Brahma below a gnat; the wise therefore abandon doubt and worship Rama. The Sanskrit verse affirms that those who worship Hari cross what is exceedingly hard to cross.

Bhushundi says he has told Hari's incomparable story in both expansion and summary according to his understanding. Its scriptural conclusion is simply to worship Rama and set every other concern aside: whom should one serve after abandoning Raghupati, who shows affection even to a fool like him? Garuda is the form of realization and not deluded; his holy question, dear to Shuka, Sanaka, Shiva and other sages, is an act of extraordinary kindness. Even a moment of saintly company is rare in the world. Bhushundi asks Garuda to reflect: though the lowest of birds and impure in every way, he has been made famous and pure by the Lord. He feels blessed despite every deficiency because Rama regarded him as his own servant and granted a saintly meeting. He has spoken according to his capacity and hidden nothing, though no one can fathom the ocean of Raghunayaka's deeds.

Remembering Rama's many hosts of virtues, wise Bhushundi rejoices again and again. The Vedas praise the Lord's immeasurable strength, splendour and sovereignty only by saying 'not this, not this.' Raghuraya's feet are worshipped by Shiva and Brahma, yet the supremely gentle Lord has shown grace to Bhushundi. He has neither heard of nor seen such a nature; whom could Garuda count equal to Raghupati? Practitioners, perfected beings, liberated and detached people, poets, scholars, grateful renunciants, yogis, heroes, severe ascetics, knowers, dharma-devoted scholars and realized sages cannot cross without serving his Lord. Bhushundi repeatedly bows to Rama. Even a mass of sin like himself becomes pure on seeking refuge; he bows to the Imperishable.

Garuda says Bhushundi's words, steeped in the nectar of Raghubira-devotion, have fulfilled his life. New love for Rama's feet has arisen and every Maya-born calamity has gone. Bhushundi became his boat across the ocean of delusion and gave him many joys; unable to repay the benefit, Garuda repeatedly bows at his feet. No one is more fortunate than this Rama-loving sage whose every desire is fulfilled. Saints act for everyone's welfare like trees, rivers, mountains and earth. Poets compare a saint's heart to butter but do not fully grasp it: butter melts from its own heat, while holy saints melt at another's suffering. Garuda says his life and birth have borne fruit and all doubt has gone through Bhushundi's grace; he asks always to be regarded as Bhushundi's servant. Shiva tells Uma that the lord of birds says this repeatedly.

Shiva says he has told the supremely holy history whose hearing releases the bonds of becoming and awakens love for the lotus of Rama's feet, the wish-fulfilling tree of the surrendered and mass of compassion. The sins born of mind, action and speech depart from those who listen with attentive ears and mind. Pilgrimage and every discipline—yoga, detachment, skill in knowledge, many acts of dharma, vows, gifts, restraint, self-control, repetition, austerity, sacrifices, compassion for beings, service to Brahmins and guru, learning, humility, discernment and greatness—all culminate, as the Vedas declare, in devotion to Hari. Scripture sings that devotion to Raghunatha, but only a rare person receives it through Rama's grace.

Only one whose mind is coloured by Rama's feet is truly all-knowing, virtuous, discerning, learned, generous, devoted to dharma and a saviour of the lineage. Such a person is truly skilled in ethics, supremely wise, understands scripture's conclusion, is poet, scholar and steadfast warrior, and worships Raghubira without deceit. Blessed is the land where the Ganga flows; blessed the woman who follows the vow of fidelity; blessed the king who governs with justice and the Brahmin who does not leave the proper dharma. Blessed is wealth directed first toward the highest end, and mature the understanding devoted to merit. Blessed is the moment of saintly company, and blessed the Brahmin birth with unbroken devotion.

Shiva says he has told the story according to his understanding, though he had earlier kept it hidden; seeing Uma's great love, he related Raghupati's story. It should not be told to a foolishly obstinate person who will not listen attentively to Hari's play, nor to the greedy, angry or lustful person who does not worship the Lord of moving and unmoving creation. It must never be recited to one hostile to Brahmins, even if that person is a king like Indra. Those who deeply love saintly company are entitled to Rama's story, as are those who love the guru's feet, follow right conduct and serve Brahmins. It gives special joy to one for whom Shri Raghuraya is dearer than life.

Shiva tells Girija that the Rama-story he has narrated calms Kali's impurity, cleanses the mind's defilement and is the life-restoring herb for the disease of transmigration, as the Vedas and sages sing. Its seven beautiful flights of steps form the path of Raghupati-devotion. Only one who receives Hari's extraordinary grace can set foot upon this way. Those who abandon deceit and sing the story attain their heartfelt aims; those who tell, hear or gladly approve it cross the ocean of becoming as though it were the water in a calf's hoofprint. Hearing the entire story, Girija loves it deeply and says her doubts have departed by Shiva's grace and fresh love for Rama's feet has arisen.

The auspicious dialogue of Shiva and Uma produces happiness, ends sorrow, breaks worldly bondage, dispels doubt, delights devotees and is dear to the good. Nothing is dearer to Rama's worshippers. Tulsidas says he has sung the lovely holy story according to his understanding through Raghupati's grace. In Kali there is no other discipline—yoga, sacrifice, repetition, austerity, vow or ritual worship—equal to remembering Rama, singing of Rama and continually hearing his virtues. Poets, Vedas, saints and Puranas proclaim his great vow to purify the fallen; abandoning crookedness, worship him, for who has failed to find the goal through Rama-devotion? The first song asks the foolish mind who has not been saved by Rama: the courtesan, Ajamila, hunter, vulture, elephant and many sinners were carried across; Abhiras, Yavanas, Kiratas, Khasas, Chandalas and others deemed deeply sinful become pure by uttering the name once. The second says those who tell, hear and sing this ornament of Raghu's line wash off Kali's and the mind's impurity and go effortlessly to Rama's abode; whoever holds these one hundred and five beautiful chaupais in the heart has the five cruel disorders born of ignorance removed by Raghubara. The third praises the beautiful, wise, compassionate Rama who loves the helpless: he alone acts without self-interest and grants liberation; by the slightest grace from him even slow-witted Tulsidas found supreme rest, and nowhere is a Lord equal to Rama. The closing couplets plead: none is as destitute as Tulsidas and none as friendly to the destitute as Raghubira, so may the jewel of Raghu's line remove the terrible fear of becoming; as woman is dear to the lustful and money to the greedy, may Rama remain ceaselessly dear to him. The Sanskrit colophon says Tulsidas rendered this Manas in the vernacular for constant devotion to Rama's lotus feet and to calm his own inner darkness, following the difficult Ramayana formerly composed by the great poet Shiva; those who devoutly immerse themselves in this pure, auspicious, merit-giving Ramcharitmanas—which removes sin and Maya's delusion and grants realization and devotion—are not scorched by the terrible rays of worldly downfall.

words: for constant devotion to Shri Rama's lotus feet
removing the impurity of Maya and delusion
a flood of the water of love
those who immerse themselves with devotion
by the terrible rays of worldly downfall
